items.headline: UK Sep CPI verified: 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky; PPI +4.6% vs 4.3%) — GBP/USD +0.1% to 1.339, EUR/GBP 83.80p strongest in 17 months; Nov-5 BoE ~96-98%, no repricing
BoC Oct-28 hike ~90-95%: CORRA OIS 95% (BlueGamma, Oct 21); LSEG ~85% (Oct 20); Spectra 83.9% — firmed toward a near-done deal from ~30% Friday

France 10Y OAT hits 5.00% (first since Jul 2002); OAT-Bund ~157-160bp Wednesday (widest since the 2009-11 crisis); revenue-section first reading postponed to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg)
BoE Gov Bailey fireside chat today 2pm London (8:00am CT) — topic central bank independence; first BoE voice post-CPI

Brent +1.1% ~$110.03 in Asia (Reuters); Tuesday $112→$106 whipsaw on unconfirmed Qatar/Pakistan mediation reports, then retraced; WTI (Dec) ~$99.18 — Brent-WTI ~$11.20 keeps the geopolitical premium intact

Houthis DENY launching drones toward Medina today; Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drones over Medina and the Eastern region — contradictory wire-level claims; Shabwa camp toll 73 (Reuters, Oct 21)

PBoC first overnight reverse repo: sold ¥80bn overnight (zero 7-day; ¥56bn 7-day matured) — net inject ¥24bn; yuan midpoint 6.7192 (strongest since Feb 2023); Commerzbank: operational tweak, no FX impact
DXY ~101.76 (near 3-week low); dipped to 101.50 Tuesday (lowest since Oct 1) — drifting on UK/NZ inflation and steady yields
Gold ~$4,115 (-0.2%, 4th straight down day) — trading December-hike odds (~90%), not oil headlines
NZ Q3 CPI tonight 4:45pm CT (0.8% q/q, 3.8% y/y fc; RBNZ proj 3.9%) — the Oct-28 RBNZ decider; hike ~80-81% to 3.00%, December second hike ~50%
France to deploy military for weekend protests; curfews 'where required' — EUR/USD pinned ~1.1220 on fiscal unrest
Houthis claim attacks on Aramco Yanbu, Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh/Abha airports — unverified by Reuters; Saudi silent
Supertanker catches fire on mine strike south of Hormuz (IRGC Navy claim via Iranian media); 18+ vessel attacks in 2 weeks (Kpler)
Japan September trade deficit -¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn forecast; exports +16.7% y/y miss (+20.1% exp); mineral-fuel imports +39.4%
API: US crude stocks -4.93M barrels (vs ~1.3M draw exp); second straight big draw; EIA due today
BoE's Greene: wage disinflation 'has stalled at levels above those consistent with inflation at 2%' — hawkish into Nov 5
GBP/USD +0.66% to 1.339 intraday as UK jobs beat (unemp 4.7% vs 4.9%) locks in Nov 5 BoE hike; DXY -0.27% to 101.69
US pending home sales -7.3% m/m in September (vs -0.4% fcst); index 66.0 = record low since 2001
GDT Event 414: WMP +4.4% ($3,760/t), SMP +3.4% ($3,975/t) — powder-led firm read
US housing starts 1.221M SAAR miss (vs 1.30M fcst, -7.4% y/y); permits 1.400M in line; 30-yr mortgage 7.40%
German producer prices rise 6.7% y/y in September, beating 6.2% consensus
China leaves loan prime rates steady for 17th month (1y 3.00%, 5y 3.50%), as expected; Pan flags loan-pricing reform
